description: Where faults concentrate across GPU, host and telemetry domains. Canonical owner of the cross-domain rack and tray scorecards. Holds no single-domain copies by design: GPU Health, Executive, Node Deep Dive and Business Insights own those datasets.

options.content:
Cross-Domain Impact — blast radius by rack and tray

This page answers one question: where do the faults concentrate? It deliberately holds no single-domain copies — GPU health lives on GPU Health, tray availability on Executive, host pressure on Node Deep Dive, power on Business Insights. What is here instead are the scorecards that put every domain in one row, so a fault cluster in one rack is visible as a rack problem rather than a GPU problem. A GPU hardware fault means a latched XID, a volatile ECC error or an uncorrectable row remap. All data is tray-side telemetry: node exporter and DCGM on ~1 900 GB300 trays. A tray is counted as silent when its newest sample in the window is over five minutes old — not when up==0. On this stack a tray that stops answering has its scrape target withdrawn rather than reporting zero, so an up==0 tile reads 0 while whole racks are dark.
